author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Ten years after the UK voted to leave the EU, polls suggest most Britons now say it was a mistake. Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he is not ruling out another referendum after the next election.

Al Jazeera’s Rory Challands asked people who voted for Brexit whether they would vote the same way again.

Tim Jones, a Lincolnshire cheesemaker who voted Leave, says Brexit has harmed his business, with lost customers and higher costs.

In Stoke-on-Trent, known as the “Brexit capital” after nearly 70 percent voted to leave in 2016, the promised rewards have yet to materialise. Boarded-up shops and delayed projects point to urban neglect.

Burnham says any change to the UK’s relationship with Europe must lift up places that have been left behind. Surveys by YouGov and other pollsters suggest most Britons think leaving was the wrong call and a majority would vote to rejoin.

Al Jazeera’s Rory Challands reports from the Midlands of England.

Subscribe to our channel: http://bit.ly/AJSubscribe
title: Ten years after Brexit vote, would voters choose the same again?

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
For the Munduruku people of the Brazilian Amazon, the fish they depend on for survival have become poisoned with mercury. As soaring gold prices drive illegal miners deeper into the rainforest, mercury used to extract the gold contaminates rivers and enters the food chain, putting entire communities at risk.

In Blood Gold, Fault Lines meets Indigenous families confronting the health consequences of illegal mining and fighting to protect their land. With rare access to an illegal mine, senior correspondent Josh Rushing witnesses how mercury is used to extract gold. He meets a researcher documenting the contamination of Indigenous communities and a federal prosecutor working to stop the mercury trade. The film examines why illegal mining persists despite government crackdowns and who pays the price for the world’s appetite for gold.

Director and Producer: Mauricio Monteiro Filho 
Senior Correspondent: Josh Rushing
Senior Producer: Nic Pollock
Executive Producer: Laila Al-Arian
Editor:
title: The Munduruku’s fight for survival in the Brazilian Amazon | Fault Lines Documentary

description:
The International Court of Justice has ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during the military’s 2017 crackdown, ordering steps towards reparations and return, though enforcement remains uncertain. The landmark judgment has implications for other genocide cases, including South Africa’s case against Israel over Gaza. 

Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen reports from The Hague.
